warnings: All figures transcribed from Thai numerals (๐-๙) on a grayscale/low-contrast printed table -- individual digit misreads are possible despite reasonable confidence; recommend spot-checking against the source if these figures feed into any downstream cost model.

House #6's row shows ฐานรากแผ่ (spread footing, 1,227,000 baht) MORE EXPENSIVE than ฐานรากเสาเข็ม (pile foundation, 1,102,000 baht) -- the reverse of every other row on this table (pile foundation is consistently pricier elsewhere, as expected since piling adds cost). This exact same anomaly pattern (one house's pricing reversed) was also flagged in house #3's equivalent reference table for a different house number -- worth a consolidated human review across all houses' pricing tables rather than treating each as an isolated one-off.

RESOLVED_2026-07-19: the #10 anomaly warning that stood here guessed 'possibly a digit misread of 2,145,000' -- that guess was CORRECT. 8x zoom across all 4 copies shows ๒,๑๔๕,๐๐๐/๒,๐๓๕,๐๐๐; values fixed, the 2026-07-16 zoom conclusion (๒,๙๔๕,๐๐๐) misread ๑ as ๙. Also fixed per the same pass: #1 pile 1,020,000, #2 pile 1,460,000, #3/#8 sizes 156, #4 spread 1,824,000 (this house's own row).

NORMALIZED_2026-08-02(r5b): the 10-design series price table was stored in a different shape in every house (house_catalog / house_series / elements rows / material_list categories). Unified to series_price_table[] — the form houses 08/09/10 already use — under pattern misc. Field renames only; every value that had to change to match the item-37 consensus (verified at 8x zoom on 5 copies) keeps its old value in *_printed_as with a RE-CORRECTED flag. This file previously escaped the item-37 correction round (สิ่งที่ต้องแก้ item 55 syndrome: the log said fixed, the file was not).
